task: round16 verify PC16-04 (43/44 read trigger timeout)
reason: The gap is real. The CONTEXT 06:19Z entry (3) and R15-A5 fire the 43/44 read only at 'the first poll.log header with both refs terminal' and set no timeout. Entry (4) needs L_hi <= 9.0 h (first COMPLETE header by 14:28:13Z / 14:28:22Z), and it accepts an 'ERROR/unscored' other rung without saying WHEN a rung counts as unscored. A fixed cutoff closes a post-hoc window: without one, a late rung's score could still decide the smoothness clause for the other rung. The fix is still pre-score. There is no CONTEXT entry after 07:41Z, and the ledger at 08:40:46Z shows both refs PENDING; the earliest terminal header is ~12:10Z. It is a log line, not a mechanism: R8 does not apply, nothing is submitted or built, and the byte-identical and fail-soft rules do not apply. Three corrections. (1) 'Wait with no end' is overstated. The safetail 9.5 h deadline and Kaggle's 12 h limit force COMPLETE or ERROR by ~17:30Z unless Kaggle itself hangs, and the finals deadline (29 Sep 20:00Z) leaves slack. So the benefit is determinism and pre-registration, not unblocking. (2) The '14:30Z header' does not exist as written. poll.log headers come every ~10 min and drift ~+2 s per poll (07:30:34 ... 08:40:46Z), so the one near 14:30 lands at ~14:31-14:32Z. The rule should name the first header at or after 14:28:22Z. That loses nothing: the header before it is ~14:21Z, and any ref first COMPLETE later already fails L_hi <= 9.0 h. (3) If the poll.log watcher itself stops, the timeout never fires, so a wall-clock fallback is needed. Value on private: zero score effect; this is procedural hygiene only.
fix: Append to the PC16-02 composition line, before any poll.log header shows 56598763 or 56598765 terminal: 'READ TRIGGER (R15-A1 (3)/(4) addendum, pre-score): the first poll.log header with both refs terminal, or the first header at or after 14:28:22Z, whichever comes first. If poll.log has no header by 14:40Z (date -u), run one ListSubmissions read, log it, and use it as the header. A ref not COMPLETE/ERROR at that header is UNSCORED for R15-A1 (4): it already fails its own L_hi <= 9.0 h and satisfies the other rung's ERROR/unscored clause. A later score of it is logged as info only (DC-dose / private-read v2) and never re-opens V*_C or the pair.' Commit and push as the user, together with the PC16-02 line.
realistic_gain: 0 on public and private score. It removes an undefined read time and a post-hoc lever (a late rung's score deciding the other rung's eligibility) at the cost of one log line. It matters only if a ref runs past ~9 h, which is unlikely: 43/44 latencies should be ~6.7-7.6 h, like #37/#38/exp70b.
